answers.answer: Straight answer: my sole hard anchor, Vardhman FY20 RM=54%-of-revenue, is an INTEGRATED-SPINNER figure, and I must not smuggle it in as though it measured the entrant's non-integrated knit-garment unit. My spec is explicit that ONLY the material-dominance LINE is a hard [FACT]; the knit-garment shares (~50-65% yarn / ~15-25% labour / ~5-10% power) are LABELLED [ESTIMATE] order-of-magnitude bands, not measured knit averages. So the 54% grounds DIRECTION (yarn/material dominates this cluster's cost), which transfers qualitatively because both spinning and knit-garment are yarn-intensive; it does NOT ground the precise knit share. On the counterfactual: if the true knit-garment yarn share were 45% rather than ~60%, does 'edge can never be cost' survive? YES — because that conclusion does NOT actually depend on yarn being any specific share. It depends on a DIFFERENT structural fact set in my spec: the compliant entrant carries the full compliance premium (EPF/ESI loading, GST inverted-duty trap, effluent-if-dyeing, full statutory wages) while competing against off-roll price-setters who shed those, AND cannot replicate the incumbents' vertical integration / captive power / scale (the moat mirror), AND inherits the spinner's market-yarn price with no captive-yarn discount. Even at 45% material share the entrant still pays market yarn PLUS the compliance premium PLUS the sub-scale penalty, so it still cannot win on cost. GAP the questioner correctly presses: my spec does NOT state a MINIMUM material-dominance threshold, because — on honest inspection — the 'edge can never be cost' verdict is not actually gated on a material-share number at all; it is gated on the compliance-premium + moat-mirror + no-captive-integration facts. My spec never says this cleanly, so the load-bearing logic looks like it rides on the 54% when it really rides on the moat mirror. [FACT for the 54% anchor; ESTIMATE for all knit shares; the 'no minimum threshold needed' logic is IMPLICIT, not stated]

My spec flags the CAD/flat-knit-programmer as a bottleneck 'relevant to the AI-design pipeline' (capabilities #4) but never states 'AI is a multiplier not a substitute' or 'AI-design->knit-program autonomy is [UNKNOWN], test don't assume.' YES, [UNKNOWN] — but I state that on borrowed authority; the veto belongs to machines + design, and I must ROUTE the 'AI replaces the programmer/linker' claim to them rather than adjudicate it in my lane. answers.answer: Stating the DOWNSIDE of my lone tailwind honestly. The mesh's DOWNSIDE, which my spec under-states: when a garment crosses many tiny vendors (spin -> knit -> link -> finish) with NO single owner, QC ACCOUNTABILITY fragments — there is no one throat to choke for a defect, hand-offs multiply defect-injection points, and the linker-quality reputation (which my glossary 'linking / linker bottleneck' says is 'where a small unit's quality reputation is won or lost') is exposed precisely because linking is one more subcontracted step in the chain rather than an owned operation. So the mesh is a coordination TAILWIND and a QC-fragmentation LIABILITY at once; I must NOT sell it as an unqualified good. Now — is that QC break MINE to own or must I route it? It is SHARED: the STRUCTURAL fact that the mesh is fragmented (many micro-vendors, no single owner) IS my lane (I own the agglomeration/moat read and can flag that job-work is 'flexible but QC-fragmented', per SCOPE_GLOSSARY sec 9). But the QC REMEDY — the own/demand/buy QC posture, the AQL incoming-inspection the brand owns, the willingness-to-reject gate, how to hold quality across fragmented vendors — is OUT of my lane (boundaries route QC to T5) and OWNED by quality_qc_strategist. So: I flag the fragmentation as a cost of my tailwind and ROUTE the QC-accountability remedy to quality_qc (T5).
